newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Smiths profits seen gaining height.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Smiths profits seen gaining height.

text.p: LONDON, Oct 11 (REUTER) - Smiths Industries Plc is expected to show a further advance in profits next Wednesday, boosted by a characteristic mix of organic growth and acquisitions in its medical and industrial divisions.

Analysts are forecasting pretax profits of 159-165 million stg for the year to end-July, up from 138 million stg last time, with the dividend expected to be raised 11 percent to 16p on earnings per share up 16 percent at 36.4 pence.
But analysts say the main attraction for investors who have sent the share price soaring this year is the avionics division.
Currently subdued, the division is expected to roar into life now that civil aircraft producers are starting to crank up production rates in response to increased orders from airlines.

The share price has risen by a third to 770p from 580p since Smiths reported record results a year ago, putting the share on a prospective p/e of 18 and yield of 2.8 percent based on current full-year forecasts.

Chairman Roger Hurn warned in April that rescheduling of avionics deliveries following a strike late last year at Boeing, its biggest customer, was likely to have "a modest financial impact" on its aerospace division in the second half.

But overall he said prospects for the division continued to brighten as Boeing has announced a series of major new orders this year for which Smiths has large avionics supply contracts, and the aircraft giant is also stepping up production rates.

Hurn said it remained to be seen whether aerospace would recover its position as Smiths' most profitable division once the market picked up, as the two other divisions were set to continue their advance through increased sales and acquisitions.
"What I do expect is for them to continue to storm ahead and for aerospace to begin its recovery phase in the not too distant future," he said in April.
In the half year Aerospace profits edged up to 17.2 million stg from 16.4 million last time, on sales down 1.9 million stg at 171.4 million stg.

Medical Systems, which specialises in single-use products and surgical equipment, made an operating profit of 31.6 million stg, up from 26.3 million stg last time on sales up 13 percent at 145.9 million stg.
At Industrials, where products range from flexible tubing to electrical switches, operating profits rose 33 percent to 21.6 million stg on sales up 23.7 percent at 148.9 million.

Hurn said the company's gearing was negligible and so the strategy of making bolt-on acquisitions was likely to continue whenever the right opportunities arose. Net debt was 13.5 million stg at the end of January.
